data.title: bn-38i7: Implement the optional managed guide block and example harness

data.body: [MEDIUM] An interrupted append can leave ownership markers that prevent an identical retry. write_all can append a prefix and then return an error, and the next init treats the partial block as pre-existing ambiguity. I verified this in a fresh local fixture with an existing 131072-byte AGENTS.md and a process file-size limit of 131120 bytes. The first guide install exited 7 with a committed binding and appended 48 bytes, ending with a truncated digest marker. After removing the limit, the identical command exited 6 and preserved those 48 bytes. Make the existing-file update all-or-nothing or make partial writes recoverable without truncating bytes from another writer. Add a short-write or interruption test that verifies the same-input retry and preservation of the original bytes.

[MEDIUM] The append delimiter comes from a snapshot an external writer can change after the last stat check. If the read snapshot ends with two newlines, the generated addition starts with the marker itself. A concurrent editor append without a trailing newline between ensure_current and write_all causes the marker to attach to that editor line. The post-write check returns ambiguous after the malformed install is already present, and a retry refuses it again. The directory flock serializes Scourge installers only. Ensure a valid boundary for an append regardless of preceding user bytes, and cover this interleaving without overwriting the other writer.

data.body: Fixed: A complete replacement is written and fsynced under a temporary name before publication. The RLIMIT_FSIZE process regression forces a short staged write, checks the original inode and every byte, and then installs successfully with identical argv.

Fixed: A staged replacement always places two line breaks before the opening marker. The installer rechecks the original descriptor, inode, metadata, and exact bytes immediately before the rename and retries a changed snapshot. A deterministic append during staging verifies both the appended user bytes and the complete guide. Init help documents the limit for uncooperative writers that retain the old inode after replacement.

The focused external-append witness passed with two attempts and exact user-byte preservation. Init help addresses writers holding the old inode.
